findings: No sustained arrhythmia. No pauses greater than 2 seconds. No AV block.

csf.interpretation: Unremarkable CSF. Normal cell count, protein, and glucose.

ct.impression: No acute intracranial abnormality. No haemorrhage, mass, hydrocephalus, or large-territory infarct.

findings: Structurally normal heart. No intracardiac thrombus or vegetation. No pericardial effusion.

findings.description: Indication: first language aura at 55 with white matter disease; familial NOTCH3 c.544C>T p.(Arg182Cys) reported in a maternal cousin.
Technique: Sanger sequencing of NOTCH3 exons 2-24 (the exons encoding the 34 EGF-like repeats), with targeted confirmation of the familial variant.

Result: heterozygous NOTCH3 c.544C>T p.(Arg182Cys), exon 4, a cysteine-altering variant in an EGF-like repeat; classified pathogenic (ACMG/AMP). It is the variant reported in the family. No other cysteine-altering variant detected.

output.impression: Heterozygous pathogenic NOTCH3 c.544C>T p.(Arg182Cys) cysteine-altering variant. This genotype confirms a diagnosis of CADASIL.

findings.result: 7th percentile (below average); learning reduced, recognition better than free recall.
Independent in all instrumental activities; working part-time.

output.impression: Reduced verbal memory and processing speed with low-average executive function and normal language and visuospatial function; a subcortical-pattern mild cognitive impairment. Criteria for dementia are not met.

output.query: CADASIL migraine with aura acute treatment vasoconstrictors

results.finding: Migraine with aura occurs in about a fifth to a third of patients and is often the first manifestation, usually in early adulthood; ischaemic events, mood disturbance, apathy and cognitive decline follow. Diagnosis rests on a cysteine-altering NOTCH3 variant or granular osmiophilic material on skin biopsy.
results.source: Chabriat H, Joutel A, Dichgans M, Tournier-Lasserve E, Bousser MG. CADASIL. Lancet Neurol 2009;8:643-653

results.finding: No evidence contraindicates triptans in CADASIL, but expert recommendations advise against vasoconstrictive acute migraine drugs (triptans, ergot derivatives) as first-line treatment and allow them only as a second or third choice; the evidence is limited to expert opinion and case series.
results.source: VASCERN (ERN Rare Vascular Diseases). Do's and Don'ts: CADASIL. April 2023

output.summary: Migraine with aura is a frequent early manifestation of CADASIL, and expert consensus discourages vasoconstrictive acute migraine drugs in the disease.

action_criteria.label: Optional: literature on migraine with aura and its treatment in CADASIL

prohibited_recommendations: Do not prescribe triptans or ergot derivatives for his attacks: his MRI shows an old lacunar infarct (cerebral infarction is a label contraindication to triptans), and in CADASIL vasoconstrictive migraine drugs are not a first-line acute treatment (VASCERN CADASIL recommendations, 2023)
Do not start anticoagulation without a compelling independent indication such as atrial fibrillation: the arteriopathy of CADASIL raises the risk of intracerebral haemorrhage
required_recommendations: Explain the diagnosis: CADASIL confirmed by the familial NOTCH3 variant, with migraine with typical (language) aura as a manifestation of the disease and mild subcortical cognitive impairment
Treat attacks with aspirin 900 mg or an NSAID such as naproxen 500 mg, with an antiemetic (for example metoclopramide 10 mg); no preventive is needed at about one attack a year

Treat vascular risk factors to secondary-prevention targets for established small-vessel disease: increase antihypertensive treatment (BP 136/82 mmHg on amlodipine 5 mg) towards a clinic target below 130/80 mmHg, continue the statin and remain a non-smoker

Refer to clinical genetics: explain autosomal dominant inheritance (each of his three adult children has a 50% chance of carrying the variant) and offer the children counselling and, if they wish, predictive testing, including the option not to test
Arrange cognitive follow-up with repeat neuropsychological assessment in 12 months

avoided_actions.rationale: Head CT adds nothing to MRI here: it is insensitive to the white matter pattern and the lacune that answer the question.
Lumbar puncture is not indicated: there is no suspicion of subarachnoid haemorrhage, infection or inflammation, and CSF does not diagnose CADASIL.
Echocardiography is not indicated: there has been no clinical stroke or embolic event, and PFO screening is not part of the migraine or CADASIL work-up.
Ambulatory cardiac monitoring is not indicated: there is no cardioembolic event and the attacks are migraine aura.
MR angiography is not indicated: CADASIL is an arteriolar disease that MRA does not show, and there is no thunderclap headache or suspected large-artery disease.

accepted: CADASIL (NOTCH3 R182C confirmed) with migraine with aphasic aura and early vascular cognitive impairment — aphasic episodes are CADASIL-associated migraine with aura
cerebral autosomal dominant arteriopathy with subcortical infarcts and leukoencephalopathy

differential.key_features: Against: stereotyped 15-25 minute language disturbance followed each time by a 10-14 hour migrainous headache, conscious throughout; no acute infarct on MRI. The old right putaminal lacune is clinically silent and cannot explain aphasia.
Against: pathogenic NOTCH3 variant shared with a maternal cousin; anterior temporal pole and external capsule involvement are not typical of hypertensive disease, and his hypertension is mild.

Against: the maternal family history is of strokes with dementia; neuropsychology shows a subcortical profile (processing speed, verbal learning) with normal language and visuospatial function; no disproportionate medial temporal atrophy on MRI; NOTCH3 variant found.
Against: no relapses of demyelinating type; the white matter pattern (anterior temporal poles, external capsules, lacune) is vascular, not demyelinating.

Maternal line with early strokes and dementia and a cousin with NOTCH3 p.Arg182Cys indicate autosomal dominant small-vessel disease
MRI: white matter hyperintensities in both anterior temporal poles and external capsules with an old putaminal lacune
NOTCH3 c.544C>T p.(Arg182Cys), the familial cysteine-altering variant, confirms CADASIL

findings.result: Three attacks in 3 years, the first at age 55. No earlier history of migraine or other recurrent headache.

Expressive language disturbance only: noun-finding failure with paraphasias and circumlocution. By his own account it develops over several minutes; his family perceive the start as abrupt. No visual, sensory, motor or brainstem symptoms.
15-25 minutes per attack, with full recovery of speech each time; conscious and aware throughout.
Each attack is followed within about 15 minutes by a severe (8/10) right-sided pulsating headache with nausea and photophobia lasting 10-14 hours.

Maternal line: mother with multiple strokes and dementia, died at 65; maternal uncle with strokes in his 50s; maternal cousin with genetically confirmed CADASIL (NOTCH3 p.Arg182Cys). Paternal line unaffected.
Treated mild hypertension (amlodipine 5 mg) and hypercholesterolaemia (atorvastatin 20 mg); non-smoker; 8-10 units of alcohol a week.
Paracetamol 1 g as needed for the headaches. No triptan or ergot used.
Normal language, cranial nerves, power, reflexes, sensation, coordination and gait. MoCA 28/30 (orientation 1, delayed recall 1). BP 136/82 mmHg.

Onset after 50 (first aura at 55): present. Isolated language aura: present. Family history of early strokes and dementia with a confirmed hereditary arteriopathy: present. Systemic symptoms, neoplasia, deficit outside the aura, thunderclap onset, positional or Valsalva trigger, papilloedema and painful eye: absent.

clinical_assessment.impression: The attacks fulfil ICHD-3 1.2 criteria A-C for migraine with typical (language) aura: 3 attacks, 4 of 6 characteristics. Criterion D is not met at this stage: a first aura at 55, an isolated language aura and a maternal history of early strokes, dementia and confirmed CADASIL require exclusion of a secondary cause (ICHD-3 6.8.1, headache attributed to CADASIL).

scores.ICHD-3 criterion C characteristics met: 4 of 6 (gradual development, 5-60 min duration, unilateral (aphasia counts as unilateral), headache within 60 min)

alternatives: Aspirin 900 mg or an NSAID (for example naproxen 500 mg), with an antiemetic such as metoclopramide 10 mg
contraindications: Triptans and ergot derivatives in CADASIL: no evidence contraindicates triptans, but expert recommendations advise against vasoconstrictive drugs as first-line acute treatment and allow them only as a second or third choice (VASCERN CADASIL recommendations, 2023). Triptans remain contraindicated after cerebral infarction.
Triptans are also contraindicated after ischaemic stroke or TIA and in uncontrolled hypertension.
interactions: Triptans + amlodipine: no pharmacokinetic interaction listed.
sumatriptan.proposed: Sumatriptan or another triptan for acute migraine, with amlodipine 5 mg, atorvastatin 20 mg and paracetamol as needed
sumatriptan.summary: No pharmacokinetic interaction with his current medicines; triptans and ergots are avoided in CADASIL because they are vasoconstrictors.
warnings: NSAIDs: occasional use for acute headache is acceptable; regular use can raise blood pressure and blunt the effect of antihypertensives.

additional_observations: Technique: non-contrast 3 T brain MRI with T1, T2, FLAIR, DWI/ADC and susceptibility-weighted imaging.
Comparison: outside brain MRI 18 months earlier; white matter changes and the putaminal lacune are unchanged; no new lesion.
No restricted diffusion. No microbleeds on susceptibility-weighted imaging.
No disproportionate medial temporal atrophy. Ventricles and sulci normal for age. No mass.

findings.location: bilateral external capsules and periventricular white matter

mri.impression: 1. Confluent white matter hyperintensities involving both anterior temporal poles and both external capsules, with periventricular extension; this distribution is suggestive of CADASIL. 2. Old lacunar infarct in the right putamen. 3. No acute infarct, no microbleeds; unchanged from the outside study.

patient.chief_complaint: Episodic word-finding difficulty and headache — new episodes beginning age 55; family strongly suspects hereditary condition

family_history: Mother: multiple strokes and dementia, died age 65. Maternal uncle: strokes in 50s. Maternal cousin: CONFIRMED CADASIL (NOTCH3 R182C mutation). No paternal family history of stroke.

patient.history_present_illness:
A 58-year-old British man presented to the neurology outpatient clinic following three episodes of transient expressive language difficulty with subsequent headache over the past 3 years. Episodes began at age 55 — the family describes it as sudden-onset for him (though he says 'gradual'). He becomes unable to recall specific nouns — paraphasias and circumlocutions — lasting approximately 15-25 minutes, followed by a severe right-sided pulsating headache 8/10 with nausea and photophobia lasting 10-14 hours. He remains fully conscious and aware throughout each episode.

His family history is striking: his mother died at age 65 with 'multiple strokes and dementia'; his maternal uncle also had 'strokes in his 50s and died young'; and one maternal cousin underwent genetic testing and was found to have CADASIL (NOTCH3 mutation R182C — exon 4 cysteine-altering mutation). The patient has never been tested.

He had a brain MRI at a peripheral hospital 18 months ago, organised by his GP after the first episode; the images have been sent for comparison but he does not know the result.

He has mild hypertension and borderline hypercholesterolaemia. He is a non-smoker. No prior history of stroke or noticeable cognitive decline; he retired as a solicitor and now works part-time as a legal consultant.
